recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Latvia sending about 20 soldiers to the Strait of Hormuz was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. This one was a genuine deployment, not a keyword-matching error like the wildfire correction below — but it's Latvia's own contribution to an international coalition maritime security mission on the other side of the world, with no connection to Russia or the Baltic region. The scoring gap that let this through (a Baltic country's own unrelated foreign deployments passing as a Baltic security signal) has been fixed. As always, the false positive stays in the historical record rather than being quietly deleted.
recent_corrections.context: Latvia plans to send about 20 soldiers to Strait of Hormuz — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-04

recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Lithuania sending firefighters to help France fight wildfires was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. Cause: a scoring bug — generic words like 'deployed' and 'reinforcements' (meant to catch real troop movements) were also matching ordinary disaster-response language. That bug, and several similar ones found in a full audit of the scoring keywords, has been fixed. The false positive stays in the historical record below rather than being quietly deleted — see our policy on this.
recent_corrections.context: Lithuania sends 32 firefighters to help France fight wildfires — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-01

recent_updates.title: Monthly and yearly summaries added, all periodic reports now evening-only
recent_updates.text: Two new periodic roundups alongside the existing daily and weekly ones: a monthly digest (past 30 days) and a yearly digest (past 365 days), both posted to the channel. Also fixed: the weekly digest was firing in the morning (~11:23 Riga) -- moved to the same ~20:00 Riga evening slot the daily report already uses, so every periodic summary now lands in the evening, never during the day.

recent_updates.title: National grid/pipeline operators added (102 -> 112 sources)
recent_updates.text: Baltic Sea undersea cable/pipeline sabotage is one of the most concrete, recurring hybrid-incident categories this project tracks -- when it happens, national grid and pipeline transmission operators are the first official announcers, ahead of any MoD/MFA/broadcaster coverage. Added electricity TSOs for all six countries and gas TSOs where a country has one distinct from its electricity operator: Elering (Estonia), AST + Conexus Baltic Grid (Latvia), Litgrid + Amber Grid (Lithuania), Fingrid + Gasgrid Finland (Finland), Svenska kraftnat (Sweden), PSE + GAZ-SYSTEM (Poland). All ten domains confirmed live before adding. 112 sources total.

recent_updates.title: 6 new volunteer-defence-force sources
recent_updates.text: Added the Baltic region's total-defence tradition — Estonia's Kaitseliit, Latvia's Zemessardze, Lithuania's KASP, Finland's MPK, Sweden's Hemvärnet, Poland's WOT — distinct from the regular armed forces we already track. A real source of mobilization/readiness news. 96 -> 102 sources.

recent_updates.title: 6 new civil-preparedness sources
recent_updates.text: Added a source category we'd missed entirely: national civil emergency/crisis-preparedness agencies (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Finland, Sweden, Poland) — the agencies behind household crisis guidance and public-warning-system tests. 90 -> 96 sources.

recent_updates.title: Instant Telegram commands again, via webhook this time
recent_updates.text: /scan, /mute, /ignore, /quietmode were removed as polling commands (~1.8h average lag on GitHub's best-effort schedule). Back now via a webhook in the baltic-monitor-push Vercel project -- Telegram delivers the command instantly instead of waiting for a scheduled poll. Two auth layers before anything runs: a Telegram webhook secret, then the sender's chat id must match the owner's exactly. See baltic-monitor-push's README for setup.

recent_updates.title: Mastodon added as a third public alert channel
recent_updates.text: A public channel for people who follow the fediverse instead of (or alongside) Telegram. Scoped identically to browser push -- only an actual WATCH/WARN or a recovery back to QUIET, never routine QUIET scans or the weekly/daily/trend reports. Opt-in via MASTODON_INSTANCE_URL and MASTODON_ACCESS_TOKEN secrets -- see README Setup.

recent_updates.title: External heartbeat added, closing a real blind spot
recent_updates.text: The Aug 6 GitHub Actions/Pages outage exposed a gap: the watchdog only notices a problem if GitHub actually runs it -- during that outage the watchdog itself sat queued for over an hour, unable to catch its own non-execution. health-check.yml now pings an external dead-man's-switch service (healthchecks.io) that alerts on its own infrastructure if a ping stops arriving, independent of GitHub or anything else this project runs on. Opt-in via a HEALTHCHECKS_PING_URL secret -- see README Setup.

recent_updates.title: Public JSON API added for the live status data
recent_updates.text: A documented, versioned read API (GET https://baltic-monitor-push.vercel.app/api/status) now sits alongside the Telegram channel, browser push, and RSS feed -- for anyone who wants to build on this data (a script, another site, a bot) without scraping HTML or depending on the landing page's own internal status.json, which can change shape whenever that page's UI needs something new. No auth, no rate limit -- same data that is already fully public on the site.

recent_updates.title: Fixed real translation gaps on the ET/LV/LT site pages
recent_updates.text: Full review of the Estonian/Latvian/Lithuanian site text against the English original. Found a real bug: the watchdog's "Attention needed" freshness message was never translated -- only the healthy "Last scan: Xh ago" pattern was, so the one unhealthy message would have shown raw English on exactly the occasion something is actually wrong. Fixed, plus a dropped clause restored in the LV/LT FAQ for parity with EN/ET. Rest of the translated text read as complete and accurate.

recent_updates.title: Historical backtest added -- and a real airspace-wording gap fixed
recent_updates.text: WARN has never fired in real scan history, so its accuracy was never actually exercised. Added two backtests modeling real, confirmed incidents (the 2023 Baltic Sea pipeline/cable sabotage, the 2025 Estonian airspace violation) run through the full scoring pipeline. Writing the second one caught a real false negative: official statements say jets "violated Estonian airspace," not the literal "airspace violation" the keyword list required, so a genuine Tier-1 statement worded that way would have been silently dropped. Fixed and locked in with a regression test. 231 tests passing.

recent_updates.title: Finland, Sweden, and Poland now covered by our richest data source
recent_updates.text: A real gap found during maintenance: GDELT's structured event data (our richest detection layer) was only ever being fetched for Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania -- Finland, Sweden, and Poland were tracked everywhere else but never included in this specific query. Fixed.

recent_updates.title: Poland's think tank added
recent_updates.text: PISM (Polish Institute of International Affairs) closes the last remaining gap -- every tracked country now has a national security/foreign-policy think tank. Total: 90 sources.

recent_updates.title: Poland's national broadcaster added
recent_updates.text: TVP World, Poland's public broadcaster's English-language international news channel, closes the last remaining gap -- every tracked country now has one. Total: 89 sources.

recent_updates.title: Poland's Foreign Ministry added
recent_updates.text: Closed the last parity gap from Poland's addition earlier -- every other tracked country already had its Foreign Ministry covered, Poland now does too. Total: 88 sources.

recent_updates.title: Corrections now reach the site immediately
recent_updates.text: Published corrections used to only update this repo's own private log -- the public site's Corrections history section wouldn't show it until the next scheduled scan happened to run, sometimes hours later. Fixed so a correction reaches the site the moment it's published.

recent_updates.title: Fixed duplicate stories in the RSS feed and site
recent_updates.text: Some flagged stories were briefly showing up twice (in feed.xml and on the site's Recent flagged items list) when the same event got re-detected under a new link. Fixed at the source and added a safety net so it can't recur.

recent_updates.title: Poland added as a tracked country
recent_updates.text: Added as a source only, not as a new relevance trigger -- a pure Poland-Russia story still needs a genuine Baltic connection to be flagged. Brings the total to 87 sources.

recent_updates.title: Fixed "sources scanned" not matching "total sources"
recent_updates.text: Two numbers on the site that should always agree were quietly drifting apart under certain conditions. Fixed so they always match.

recent_updates.title: Swedish Armed Forces added
recent_updates.text: Added to Tier 2.

recent_updates.title: Fixed a silent-hang risk in source fetching
recent_updates.text: A single unresponsive source could previously stall an entire scan indefinitely. Fixed with a hard timeout.

recent_updates.title: GDELT event classification added to item detail
recent_updates.text: Flagged items now show the structured event category and intensity score behind them, not just the headline.

recent_updates.title: Hardened keyword matching
recent_updates.text: Added word-boundary and negation checks to the scoring logic, closing a class of false-positive bugs.

recent_updates.title: Recent scan history became clickable
recent_updates.text: Every row in "Recent scans" now expands to show exactly what was checked and why, including QUIET results.

recent_updates.title: Fixed a real false positive: an unrelated overseas deployment
recent_updates.text: Latvia's own troop contribution to an international maritime mission near the Strait of Hormuz had been wrongly flagged as a Baltic-Russia signal. Fixed and logged publicly as a correction.

recent_updates.title: Two more security think tanks added
recent_updates.text: Closed a remaining per-country coverage gap in Tier 2's think-tank sources.

recent_updates.title: NATO CCDCOE and Foreign Ministries added
recent_updates.text: NATO's Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence and the three Baltic states' Foreign Ministries added as sources.

recent_updates.title: Audited every scoring keyword for false positives
recent_updates.text: After catching a real false positive (an unrelated wildfire-relief story wrongly flagged), every keyword in the scoring list was audited and hardened against similar non-security matches.

recent_updates.title: National CERT/cyber-security agencies added
recent_updates.text: Added as Tier 2 sources across the tracked countries.

recent_updates.title: Daily evening report added
recent_updates.text: A short daily summary now goes out at roughly 21:00 Riga time.

recent_updates.title: Routine all-clear scans go fully silent
recent_updates.text: A scan that finds nothing relevant no longer sends any message at all -- only a real WATCH/WARN, or a source failure, reaches the public channel.
